holidays.name: National Wildlife Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate animals big and small, from majestic elephants to the squirrel raiding your bird feeder. Fans celebrate by visiting sanctuaries, donating to conservation groups, or just watching the local wildlife with a little more respect.
holidays.origin: Founded in 2005 by animal behaviorist and pet lifestyle expert Colleen Paige, who also started National Dog Day and National Cat Day. It was chosen to honor the memory of Steve Irwin, the Crocodile Hunter, who died on September 4, 2006, and the observance became associated with his legacy.
holidays.funFact: Colleen Paige is also behind National Puppy Day, National Cat Day, and National Dog Day, making her something of an unofficial holiday queen for animals.

holidays.name: National Newspaper Carrier Day
holidays.description: A day to thank the folks who brave rain, snow, dogs, and ungodly hours to toss the news onto your porch, ideally not into the bushes. Celebrate by tipping your carrier or reading an actual paper.
holidays.origin: It commemorates September 4, 1833, when 10-year-old Barney Flaherty became the first newspaper carrier, hired by The New York Sun.
holidays.funFact: Barney Flaherty answered a newspaper ad seeking 'a number of steady men' to sell papers, and reportedly got the job because he was young and eager.

holidays.name: National Macadamia Nut Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the buttery, rich, ridiculously expensive nut that is the star of white chocolate cookies and Hawaiian souvenir boxes. Fans crack into a bag, though cracking the shell yourself takes some serious muscle.
holidays.origin: This is a food holiday celebrated by nut lovers and promoted by snack enthusiasts. Macadamias are native to Australia, but Hawaii made them famous worldwide after they were introduced there in the 1880s.
holidays.funFact: Macadamia shells are so hard that they require about 300 pounds of pressure per square inch to crack, and the nuts are highly toxic to dogs.

holidays.name: Newspaper Carrier Day's Silly Cousin: Eat an Extra Dessert Day
holidays.description: A cheerfully indulgent day that gives you permission to order a second slice of cake with absolutely no guilt. Calories are said not to count on this day, though your doctor may disagree.
holidays.origin: Eat an Extra Dessert Day is an unofficial observance spread by food bloggers and holiday calendars, and it is usually placed on September 4 as a sweet way to wrap up the start of fall.
holidays.funFact: Dessert is 'stressed' spelled backward, a favorite pun of those who celebrate this day.

holidays.name: Hobbit Day Eve
holidays.description: The day before Hobbit Day, when fans of Middle-earth start prepping for a feast of second breakfasts, pipe-weed jokes, and long-winded stories about adventures in faraway lands.
holidays.origin: Hobbit Day on September 22 marks the shared birthday of Bilbo and Frodo Baggins in J.R.R. Tolkien's works, and it was first celebrated by the American Tolkien Society in 1978. Fans often kick off festivities a few weeks early.
holidays.funFact: Tolkien said he wrote the famous first line of The Hobbit, 'In a hole in the ground there lived a hobbit', while grading exam papers, when he found a blank page and scribbled it down.
